# Current canonical 0.4.1 converter/RI integration

Tracks [Tools #59, November 17 follow-up](https://github.com/vanderpol/scap-ng-tools/issues/59#issuecomment-6955806636).
One main-based Tools PR; no old stacks or generated corpus imported.

## Audited delta and regenerated bytes

Canonical main: `5ee55288b369da26f308f40813e545b78dff2753`.
Of the **145** flat schema/mapping resources, **144 are identical** to Tools'
previous accepted canonical `4c2713b051203fe8e93570adc1ccc65b50129ae2`.
The sole change removes `profiles.items.properties.extends` from
`benchmark.schema.json`: native Profiles independently specify disabled Rules.
Benchmark/Group/Rule applicability, all Results and all capability resources
already match; no new interpretation or schema edit was needed.

The entire flat family now hashes to
`88fc59791f9cb5055d2a8dc27bb458bcf6699b5820061ce68af1a355bd33a84f`.
The production semantic pack was rebuilt through the existing generator from
that exact canonical checkout and official OVAL
`2f140ee5c5dd1ed9606fcd5afc301f6baeb48706`, not edited as JSON.
The generator now derives eight behavior records from the original XSD instead
of reading its previous pack. A regression poisons the old-pack reader and
requires two byte-identical rebuilds. All 53 generated capability contracts
and all eight behavior records remain identical; only contract identity and
canonical provenance changed. `canonical-schema-pin.json` is generator output
with exact sizes/hashes for every resource, the regenerated pack and RI closure.
The Tools editor exporter was regenerated/checked against its 236 resources;
its manifest and resource checksums were refreshed without editing editor code.

## Separate schema identities, both checked

RI merged main `dc77e33cb9cc74479622681e00ff776e2161b6ba` validates Assessment
requests with execution-family identifier
`326f82668020a717f5d3443484330f313146978292befd75c063f55b2e4e5329`.
That identity guards an **eight-resource Assessment $ref closure**, not the
current whole flat schema. The former converter emitted its flat digest into
the runner's execution-family field, causing `schema_pin_mismatch` errors even
after conversion succeeded.

The converter now emits `schema_family_sha256` for the checked RI execution
closure, with explicit `schema_family_scope: assessment_ref_closure`, and
retains the whole-schema digest separately as `flat_schema_family_sha256`.
It walks the current canonical Assessment refs, verifies the exact closure hash
`d6e3e6fde5dbacce39eef8a75285be053c85d52806517cda05eec132fc060bfd`, and
rejects missing/changed/foreign resources. The pin generator independently
compares all eight canonical resource bytes/sizes/hashes to RI main's embedded
manifest before emitting the binding. The full 145-resource validator remains
mandatory. This is an explicit execution handshake, not an old-schema loader,
digest waiver or unverified equivalence assertion. RI code is unchanged.

## Reproduce and evidence

Install this checkout with `python -m pip install -e .`, and Go **1.27.4**.
Use the canonical, OVAL and merged RI revisions above and original Self-Assertion
`e3538595c5083b9c34d937a81d319234df9bbfaa`:

```sh
scripts/qualify_p0_041.sh /canonical /oval /ri /source /new/external/output
```

The shared local/Actions lane verifies deterministic pack/pin regeneration,
executes converter regressions and the existing five-Rule Windows diagnostic,
then runs RI main's unmodified `tools/run_p0_validation.sh`: Go full tests,
race tests, vet, schema/module checks, then the complete 46-Definition runner.
The scanner receives original source identities and converted native content;
independent expected outcomes are compared afterward. The original expected
manifest SHA remains
`9a9961fc8bcdf30d2d01e9178c0b59befc5e871724c48d6fe38fd9443906ce7c`.
The eight approved malformed-Variable corrections and their three original XML
hashes are unchanged; `var:100` stays integer. Negation, aliases and source
Definition IDs are preserved. Generated runs remain outside Tools and are
uploaded by `.github/workflows/p0-canonical-qualification.yml`.

The first full corrected-handshake run matched **46/46: 44 TRUE, one FALSE
(`def:997`), one UNKNOWN (`def:337`)**, through normal RI main execution.
The final clean run on Tools `02b283c3dbe81c84532f434fbbf6d180d5eb84a8`
also matched all 46. [Checksummed external manifest](https://github.com/vanderpol/scap-ng-evidence/blob/73170a5bfca44589fe6ba3fa2c2cfeb0a3ea9793/runs/tools-p0-041/2026-11-17-02b283c/manifest.json)
and [actual Definition ledger](https://github.com/vanderpol/scap-ng-evidence/blob/73170a5bfca44589fe6ba3fa2c2cfeb0a3ea9793/runs/tools-p0-041/2026-11-17-02b283c/definition-results.csv) retain
the results. [Local validation summary](validation.json) records the pins.
287 converter tests passed with five existing fixture-dependent skips; Go
1.27.4 full/race/vet/schema/module checks and both pack/pin rebuilds passed.
This qualifies the owner's normalized source-compatibility milestone, not
original malformed OVAL equivalence, CPE scanner mappings or a product release.

- Windows Server 2016 source ZIP SHA
  `76cf6a14fefd077136d9a23a6ba4a30c82a0b254adc8cf2abd88592dc30776a8`
  now passes digest admission. Its five source-linked witnesses still have
  unsupported Input `constraints.relation` authoring. The diagnostic preserves

- Enabling all original signed-benchmark fixtures exposed 13 assertion failures
  in the historical 535-Rule conversion/inventory hash/count/negative-gate tests
  and focused conversion hash. The 296-test run is retained as **failed**;
  the identical 13 assertion failures reproduce on pre-change Tools
  `29bc686` with its approved canonical `4c2713b` snapshot. Those goldens were
  not changed to force a pass. The scoped schema/OVAL suite
  has no failures; source-benchmark requalification remains separate.
- Historical full-65/publication replay lanes remain tied to their old source

- Divergent Tools #67 `time_difference` and #53 work remain retrievable and

  not closed without exact incorporation/supersession proof.
- Hosted Actions historically fails before steps; only actual executed jobs
